text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Oil marketing firms and the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) are heading for a showdown over allegations that the private companies are hoarding fuel on a large scale.
- Lagos high court orders the release of seven detainees suspected of involvement in a 1990 coup attempt.
- Head of State General Sani Abacha visits neighbouring Niger.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says there is consensus on the need to establish a second stock exchange in Nigeria, with the administrative capital Abuja as the likely place.

- European and American firms impose increasingly strict conditions on leasing aircraft to Nigerian companies. The foreign firms are said to be afraid of leasing to Nigerians because of difficulties in the past, when local companies used the courts to stop leasing firms from retrieving their planes.
- Forum of traditional rulers set up by government. The forum aims to expand the participation of the rulers in national issues.
- Mobil plans to sell electricty to the National Electric Power Authority from a 360 megawatt power station being planned for southeastern Rivers State.
